steps.prompt: Hold up all ten fingers and fold down $3$. How many are still up? How many ways can you split your $10$ fingers into two groups?

cards.title: What is a number bond?
cards.body: A number bond is two numbers that make a whole. $3$ and $7$ are a bond to $10$ because $3 + 7 = 10$. There are only five bonds to $10$: $1 + 9$, $2 + 8$, $3 + 7$, $4 + 6$ and $5 + 5$. Learn them like your name: they are the building blocks of all mental math.

cards.title: Worked example: the ten frame
cards.problem: A ten frame has $10$ boxes. $6$ boxes have a counter. How many are empty?

steps.text: Picture the frame: two rows of $5$. The top row is full and $1$ box in the bottom row has a counter.

try.prompt: How many empty boxes are in the bottom row?

steps.text: So $4$ boxes are empty. $6$ and $4$ are a bond to $10$: $6 + 4 = 10$.
The bond also gives you a take-away fact for free: $10 - 6 = 4$.

cards.title: Worked example: hunt for the pairs

steps.text: Look before you add: $7$ and $3$ are a bond to $10$.
Add them first: $7 + 3 = 10$. Then $10 + 5 = 15$. Adding a number to $10$ is easy, so pairs that make $10$ save you work.

cards.title: Why it works
cards.body: You can add numbers in any order and get the same total: $7 + 5 + 3$ is the same as $7 + 3 + 5$. So you are allowed to pick the pairs that make $10$ first. That is a pattern, not a trick: it works every time.

prompts: Which bond to $10$ do you find hardest to remember? Make up a way to remember it.
